title: Declarative EKS headplane bootstrap Terraform module with upgrade safety & health hooks
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Problem: Our current Priv EKS provisioning is a set of ad-hoc Terraform root modules and imperative scripts that make safe rolling upgrades, preflight checks, and runtime health instrumentation brittle across accounts and customer VPCs. We need a single, declarative Terraform module that encapsulates: idempotent bootstrap of the EKS control plane components (headplane), manifested health probes and repair hooks, safe upgrade orchestration signals (preflight/canary gates), and easy observability hooks so Dedicated/Private customers get consistent behaviour during provisioning and upgrades.

Goal: Deliver a reusable Terraform module (and an accompanying lightweight controller-like bootstrapper invoked by the module) that: (1) performs idempotent control plane initialization, (2) wires KMS-protected secrets and RBAC expectations, (3) exposes preflight and rollout health checks, and (4) fails safely with human-visible diagnostics and automated rollback triggers. Module should be operator-friendly (clear inputs, outputs, examples) and compatible with Redwood Private on-prem and VPC deployment patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Module accepts a declarative 'control_plane' object to configure EKS headplane resources and returns deterministic outputs (control_plane_id, bootstrap_state_tag, kubeconfig_s3_path)
Provisioning run is idempotent: repeated terraform apply against same inputs results in no drift after initial successful apply
Upgrade flow: terraform apply that changes control plane image or instance type triggers a staged canary (configurable percent) and pauses on failing health checks
Health hooks: module installs a namespaced 'provisioning-prober' Job and CloudWatch/Prometheus exporters as configured; failing probes surface as structured diagnostic logs in the Console
KMS integration: secrets generated during bootstrap stored encrypted with customer KMS key ARN input
Automated rollback trigger: if configured, a failing canary health window reverts to previous stable control_plane_tag via an automated apply plan (documented manual approval fallback)
Docs: README with inputs/outputs, example multi-account varfile, preflight checklist, and an upgrade playbook
Unit/integration tests: terraform-compliance tests and a smoke test suite for provisioning in the priv-stage account pass in CI
technical_design: Module surface: main module at modules/control_plane with submodules: eks-cluster, bootstrapper-lambda, kms-keys, observability-bridge, preflight-validator. Keep interface small: control_plane_name, account_id, region, networking (vpc_id, subnets), kms_key_arn, operator_emails, image_tag_policies, canary_percentage, health_checks_config

Bootstrapper pattern: a lightweight Lambda (go) or container image executed via local-exec or remote-exec can be toggled. It performs in-cluster initial manifests, creates a bootstrap-state tag in S3/dynamo, and emits structured events to our Console ingest. The Lambda runs under an IAM role provisioned by the module to avoid imperative CLI dependencies.

Health model: Kubernetes readiness/liveness metrics aggregated to a 'provisioning_health' Prometheus metric exported via sidecar. Module optionally creates CloudWatch alarm or Prometheus alert that ties into Console's rollout tracing. Health thresholds are configurable in health_checks_config.

Upgrade safety: module produces a 'plan' output that enumerates changed control_plane resources and, if canary_percentage > 0, creates a temporary canary stack (namespaced) and configures traffic split by labels. A Terraform apply will pause (via a null_resource with local-exec sleep/approval hook) until probes for the canary window succeed or fail. Failure path documents an automated terraform apply with previous_tag variables.

Observability: module wires logs and metrics to the priv-central telemetry S3/Prometheus endpoints and creates a dashboard snippet (Grafana JSON) as an output artifact. Bootstrapper writes bootstrap events to S3 path documented in outputs for Console ingestion.

RBAC & KMS: module creates a constrained IAM role for bootstrapper and control-plane nodes, maps necessary RBAC roles inside cluster, and stores generated secrets encrypted under the supplied KMS key. Cross-account KMS grants are created when needed using a configurable grant template.

Testing harness: terraform targets for unit-level 'plan' assertions; a parallel integration job in CI using a small ephemeral priv-stage account to do full apply/teardown. A smoke test validates kubeconfig, node readiness, and that 'provisioning_health' metric reports healthy after bootstrap

testing_plan: Local plan validation: terraform fmt/init/plan checks in pre-commit
Unit tests: terraform-compliance rule set validating inputs/outputs and plan-only sanity checks
Integration: ephemeral priv-stage account spinning up full apply/teardown; smoke tests validate kubeconfig, node readiness, provisioning_health metric, and ability to rollback after canary failure
Chaos test (optional): induce delay in API server during canary window to validate rollback path
rollback_plan: If a canary fails health windows, the module supports an automated revert by re-applying Terraform with 'previous_control_plane_tag' input. If automated revert is disabled, operators will follow the playbook to snapshot state (S3/dynamo), scale down the canary, and restore the previous tag. All rollback operations must be executed in priv-stage before customer rollout and require explicit human approval documented in the release notes.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Lambda bootstrapper concurrency limits cause incomplete manifest application - Mitigation: reserved concurrency, exponential backoff, and fallback to remote-exec helper
Risk: KMS cross-account grants are denied by customer org policies - Mitigation: provide explicit customer-facing grant manifest and helper script to request necessary privileges
Risk: Terraform state drift when partial manifests are applied - Mitigation: use a small 'bootstrap-state' object in S3/dynamo to mark progress and make module idempotent
Risk: Observability gap during early provisioning - Mitigation: include a minimal metrics exporter and require enabling of telemetry during bootstrap in examples
notes_for_release: Introduce module as opt-in in priv-eks 2026.03. Migration guide included. Recommend a staged rollout: start with non-critical customers, validate rollback and health metrics, then enable for broader fleet. Communicate KMS requirements to customers ahead of migration.
